title: In vitro and in vivo growth alter the population dynamic and properties of a Jeryl Lynn mumps vaccine.
ehr_evidence: JL-CK vaccine was provided by the Official Medicines Control Laboratory-Prague, Czech Republic. Mu90, a clinical mumps isolate passaged four times on Vero cells, and RIT4385 were archived material held at NIBSC. African green monkey (Vero) and Madin Darby canine kidney (MDCK) cell lines were used. Neonatal rat pups were inoculated intracerebrally.
summary: Comparative genomic and phenotypic analysis of two Jeryl Lynn mumps vaccine strains to assess genetic heterogeneity, in vitro growth kinetics, and in vivo neurovirulence in neonatal rats.
key_findings: JL-CK produced 100-fold more progeny virus in Vero cells (p < 0.0001) and MDCK cells (p = 0.0365) compared to RIT4385.
Sanger sequencing identified 14 regions of heterogeneity in JL-CK, with only 4% of the population corresponding to the parental strain.
JL-CK showed significantly higher neurovirulence than RIT4385 in neonatal rats (p = 0.0035), but lower than wild-type Mu90 (p < 0.001).
In vivo passage in rat brains increased the K36R mutation frequency 9.6-fold, indicating preferential selection of the JL-CK1 variant.
study_design: Experimental laboratory study (in vitro and in vivo)
data_source_type: Laboratory experiments / Cell culture and animal model
population: Neonatal rats, Vero and MDCK cell lines
exposure_domain: Vaccine production substrate (canine kidney cells vs chicken embryo fibroblasts)
limitations: Small sample sizes for animal groups
Conflicting data between neurovirulence scores and in vivo variant frequencies
